source_refs.note: Book p. 191: 10.4 Double Angle Identities, recall of sum formulas, derivations (i) sin 2a, (ii) cos 2a three forms, (iii) tan 2a; starts below Exercise 10.2 Q15 on the same page

blocks.text: Aaj ka sabaq chhota hai magar bohat taqatwar. Double angle ka matlab hai kisi angle ka dugna, yani \(2\alpha\). Agar aap ko \(\sin 30^{\circ}\) aur \(\cos 30^{\circ}\) maloom hon, to kya aap \(\sin 60^{\circ}\) seedha nikaal sakte hain? Is sabaq ke formulas yahi karte hain. Aage chal kar half angle (10.5), triple angle (10.6) aur Exercise 10.3 ke taqreeban har sawal mein yeh formulas lagenge, is liye inhein achhi tarah samajh kar yaad kariye.

Kitab pehle woh natije yaad dilati hai jo hum 10.1.2 mein prove kar chuke hain:
\[\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta + \cos\alpha\sin\beta\]
\[\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta\]
\[\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \dfrac{\tan\alpha + \tan\beta}{1 - \tan\alpha\tan\beta}\]
Inhi se hum double angle identities is tarah hasil karte hain:

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Poora raaz ek line ka hai: \(2\alpha = \alpha + \alpha\). Yani sum formulas mein \(\beta\) ki jagah bhi \(\alpha\) rakh dein, bas. Koi naya idea nahin chahiye; double angle identities asal mein sum formulas ki ek khaas soorat (special case) hain. Is liye agar kabhi exam mein formula bhool jayein, to ghabraiye mat: sum formula likhiye, \(\beta = \alpha\) rakhiye, aur formula khud ban jayega.

(i) \(\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta + \cos\alpha\sin\beta\) mein \(\beta = \alpha\) rakhein:
\[\sin(\alpha + \alpha) = \sin\alpha\cos\alpha + \cos\alpha\sin\alpha\]
Right side ke dono terms bilkul ek jaise hain (\(\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\) aur \(\cos\alpha\sin\alpha\), sirf order alag hai, multiplication mein order se farq nahin parta). Ek jaisi do cheezein jama hon to ek ka dugna ban jata hai. Is liye

blocks.text_alt: sin 2 alpha equals 2 sin alpha cos alpha

blocks.text:
(ii) Ab \(\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta\) mein \(\beta = \alpha\) rakhein:
\[\cos(\alpha + \alpha) = \cos\alpha\cos\alpha - \sin\alpha\sin\alpha\]
\[\cos 2\alpha = \cos^{2}\alpha - \sin^{2}\alpha\]
Yeh pehli shakal hai. Ab hum chahte hain ke formula mein sirf cos ho. Is ke liye \(\sin^{2}\alpha = 1 - \cos^{2}\alpha\) rakhiye (Pythagorean identity se):
\[\cos 2\alpha = \cos^{2}\alpha - (1 - \cos^{2}\alpha)\]
\[= \cos^{2}\alpha - 1 + \cos^{2}\alpha\]
\[\cos 2\alpha = 2\cos^{2}\alpha - 1\]
Dhyan dein: \(-(1 - \cos^{2}\alpha)\) kholte waqt minus dono terms par lagta hai, is liye \(-1 + \cos^{2}\alpha\) bana, aur do \(\cos^{2}\alpha\) jama ho kar \(2\cos^{2}\alpha\) ho gaye.
Isi tarah agar formula mein sirf sin chahiye to \(\cos 2\alpha = \cos^{2}\alpha - \sin^{2}\alpha\) mein \(\cos^{2}\alpha = 1 - \sin^{2}\alpha\) rakhiye:
\[\cos 2\alpha = (1 - \sin^{2}\alpha) - \sin^{2}\alpha\]
\[\cos 2\alpha = 1 - 2\sin^{2}\alpha\]
Yani \(\cos 2\alpha\) ki teen shakal hain, aur teeno bilkul barabar hain:

blocks.text_alt: cos 2 alpha equals cos squared alpha minus sin squared alpha
cos 2 alpha equals 2 cos squared alpha minus 1
cos 2 alpha equals 1 minus 2 sin squared alpha

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Teen shakal kyun? Kyun ke har sawal mein alag cheez di hoti hai. Rule yeh hai ke wahi shakal chuniye jis mein di hui cheez ho:
sirf \(\cos\alpha\) maloom ho to \(2\cos^{2}\alpha - 1\); sirf \(\sin\alpha\) maloom ho to \(1 - 2\sin^{2}\alpha\); dono maloom hon to \(\cos^{2}\alpha - \sin^{2}\alpha\).
Aakhri do shaklon ko tarteeb badal kar likhein to do bohat kaam ke natije milte hain:
\[1 + \cos 2\alpha = 2\cos^{2}\alpha\]
\[1 - \cos 2\alpha = 2\sin^{2}\alpha\]
Yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: plus ke saath cos, minus ke saath sin. Yeh square ko hata kar seedhe cos mein badal dete hain, aur agle sabaq (10.5, half angle) ki bunyaad yahi hain.

(iii) Aakhir mein \(\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \frac{\tan\alpha + \tan\beta}{1 - \tan\alpha\tan\beta}\) mein \(\beta = \alpha\) rakhein:
\[\tan(\alpha + \alpha) = \dfrac{\tan\alpha + \tan\alpha}{1 - \tan\alpha\tan\alpha}\]
Upar \(\tan\alpha + \tan\alpha = 2\tan\alpha\), aur neeche \(\tan\alpha\cdot\tan\alpha = \tan^{2}\alpha\). Is liye

blocks.text_alt: tan 2 alpha equals 2 tan alpha over 1 minus tan squared alpha

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Is formula ki ek shart hai: \(\tan\alpha\) mojood ho aur \(\tan^{2}\alpha \ne 1\). Misal ke taur par \(\alpha = 45^{\circ}\) rakhein to neeche \(1 - 1 = 0\) aata hai, aur zero se divide nahin ho sakta. Yeh bilkul theek hai, kyun ke \(2\alpha = 90^{\circ}\) aur \(\tan 90^{\circ}\) waise bhi defined nahin.

blocks.title: Exam tip
Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin: agar \(\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5}\) aur \(\alpha\) pehle quadrant mein ho, to \(\sin 2\alpha\), \(\cos 2\alpha\), \(\tan 2\alpha\) nikaaliye.
Pehle \(\cos\alpha\): \(\sqrt{1 - \frac{9}{25}} = \frac{4}{5}\) (pehla quadrant, is liye positive). Phir \(\tan\alpha = \frac{3/5}{4/5} = \frac{3}{4}\).
\(\sin 2\alpha = 2\cdot\frac{3}{5}\cdot\frac{4}{5} = \frac{24}{25}\).
\(\cos 2\alpha = \cos^{2}\alpha - \sin^{2}\alpha = \frac{16}{25} - \frac{9}{25} = \frac{7}{25}\).
\(\tan 2\alpha = \frac{2\cdot\frac{3}{4}}{1 - \frac{9}{16}} = \frac{3/2}{7/16} = \frac{24}{7}\).
Tasdeeq: \(\frac{\sin 2\alpha}{\cos 2\alpha} = \frac{24/25}{7/25} = \frac{24}{7}\), jo \(\tan 2\alpha\) ke barabar hai. Aur \(\left(\frac{24}{25}\right)^{2} + \left(\frac{7}{25}\right)^{2} = \frac{576 + 49}{625} = 1\). Sab sahi!

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Kya \(\sin 2\alpha\) kabhi \(1\) se bara ho sakta hai, chahe \(\sin\alpha\) aur \(\cos\alpha\) kuch bhi hon? Nahin, kyun ke \(\sin 2\alpha\) bhi aakhir ek angle ka sine hai. Isi liye \(2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\) ki sab se bari value \(1\) hai (jab \(\alpha = 45^{\circ}\)). Socha tha aap ne?

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Double angle identities sum formulas mein \(\beta = \alpha\) rakhne se banti hain.
2. \(\sin 2\alpha = 2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\).
3. \(\cos 2\alpha = \cos^{2}\alpha - \sin^{2}\alpha = 2\cos^{2}\alpha - 1 = 1 - 2\sin^{2}\alpha\); jo di hui cheez ho wahi shakal chuniye.
4. \(\tan 2\alpha = \frac{2\tan\alpha}{1 - \tan^{2}\alpha}\), shart \(\tan^{2}\alpha \ne 1\).
5. \(1 + \cos 2\alpha = 2\cos^{2}\alpha\) aur \(1 - \cos 2\alpha = 2\sin^{2}\alpha\) (plus ke saath cos, minus ke saath sin).
6. Shak ho to \(\alpha = 30^{\circ}\) rakh kar check kijiye.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\sin 2\alpha = 2\sin\alpha\) likh dena. 2 angle ke andar hai, bahar nahin. Misal: \(\sin 60^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), jab ke \(2\sin 30^{\circ} = 1\). Dono barabar nahin!
2. Shaklein gadmad karna: \(2\cos^{2}\alpha - 1\) mein 1 baad mein hai, lekin \(1 - 2\sin^{2}\alpha\) mein 1 pehle. Bachne ka tareeqa: \(\alpha = 0\) rakh kar dekhiye, dono ka jawab \(\cos 0 = 1\) aana chahiye.
3. \(\tan 2\alpha\) ke denominator mein \(1 + \tan^{2}\alpha\) likh dena. Sahi \(1 - \tan^{2}\alpha\) hai, bilkul \(\tan(\alpha + \beta)\) ki tarah minus.
